facts.statement: Amounts received under a life insurance contract on the life of a terminally ill insured are treated as paid by reason of death.
facts.quote: (A) Any amount received under a life insurance contract on the life of an insured who is a terminally ill individual.

items.stem: An insured who is terminally ill receives an accelerated death benefit from her life policy. Under federal tax law, the payment is treated as:
options: Ordinary income in the year received
An amount paid by reason of the insured's death
A taxable return of the premiums paid
A policy loan that must be repaid
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 101(g)(1) treats amounts received under a life insurance contract on the life of a terminally ill insured as paid by reason of death, so they qualify for the death benefit exclusion.

facts.statement: Amounts received on the life of a chronically ill insured are also treated as paid by reason of death.
facts.quote: (B) Any amount received under a life insurance contract on the life of an insured who is a chronically ill individual.

items.stem: Besides terminally ill insureds, federal tax law also treats accelerated death benefits as paid by reason of death when the insured is:
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 101(g)(1) covers amounts received on the life of an insured who is terminally ill or chronically ill.
